comment: Cool, another $1 on Premium and it still has no lossless. Tidal and Qobuz have hi-fi for about the same money, so Spotify is asking me to pay more for a worse product. I'll keep Spotify for Connect and Discover Weekly, but this makes the gap harder to ignore.

1) They raised the price. 2) The heart button is still gone. 3) They want more money for a worse app. This is nickel and dime money grubbing, and I'd happily pay a small add-on for the heart button back but not for the rest of this mess.

not really caring about the price honestly. what matters is whether my playlists stay the way i made them and whether the enhance thing keeps dumping recs into them. raised price is annoying but i'm staying for discover weekly.
A dollar more a month for something I use every single day is still fine by me. Premium is worth every penny for ad-free listening and skips. My only real gripe is still how free users get treated.

Going from $9.99 to $10.99 is not a big deal on its own. My issue is that for the same money, Tidal and Apple Music give me lossless and I still get 320kbps. 320 is plenty on AirPods, but I'd like to see the price rise come with something I can actually hear.

Cool, more money for the same shuffle nonsense. I pay to avoid random songs getting slipped into my liked songs and I still get smart shuffle replaying the same 20 songs. Price going up without a true shuffle option is a joke. Apple Music is looking better every time this happens.

Still one of the best deals I pay for, even at $10.99. Daily listening with no ads and offline downloads is worth it. The ads are getting heavier though and they keep taking perks away, so I hope the price bump doesn't mean more of that.

Family goes from $15.99 to $16.99. Split across the household it's still pretty cheap per person and works great for us. The only thing I'd want is the duo and family setup to stay smooth through the change.

OK so the price is going up and honestly I could care less about that, Premium is still worth it for me. What I care about is the TikTok home screen that they REFUSE to revert. If it stays like that I'm cancelling my membership and stoop to Tidal or switch to Apple Music.

Premium going up a buck is fine by me. It's still the most value I get from any subscription, and the free version is too restricted to bother with. I'd cancel everything else before I touched Premium, which is saying something given how much I complain about the UI.

Didn't expect the price to go up when the app still hides my liked-song hearts on the album list. Paying more for less is a bad look. I'm already weighing Apple Music and I'll unsubscribe again if the hearts don't come back.

Spotify raised prices again while artists get fractions of a cent per stream. Where does the extra dollar go? This is why I'm on Apple Music now, and I'm not going back until they pay artists more per stream.

lol price goes up and they still shove podcasts and AI DJ at me. recommendations are garbage now and the library is buried. YouTube Music is a great deal with a strong app and I'm seriously thinking about leaving. ui changes are killing this app.

I still think Premium is a fair price for the library and the curated playlists, and Discover Weekly is still a big reason I stay. The new UI hiding discovery playlists is annoying, but a buck more a month doesn't change my decision. Spotify's algorithm still beats Apple Music's for me.

Already cancelled Premium and the renewal pop-up still shows up every time I open the app. I've tried clearing cache and reinstalling and it didn't help. I don't care about the price going up, I just want it to stop getting in the way of pausing and skipping.

Student plan going from $4.99 to $5.99 stings a bit, especially since I'm on a budget. Still way better than paying full price with Hulu included, but the Showtime removal already left a bad taste. Not sure I'd stick with it at this price.

Price is not a big deal for me. Spotify is still the most feature-rich app I've tried for radio and quick playlists with friends. Would be nicer if they brought back album radio before raising prices, but I'm not going anywhere over a buck.
Premium price going up is fine, the setup effort I put in makes it worth it to me. Still hoping Spotlight and tabs show up soon, and I'd be bummed if they remove more stuff. For now I'm staying.

Fine with the price, Premium is still worth every penny for daily music and skipping ads on podcasts while I drive. What I'm not fine with is the home screen shoving podcasts at me. Make the music come first and I'll stop complaining.

Premium going up a bit is still worth it for me, no ads, downloads and collaborative playlists with friends. Tidal does better audio at a similar price, so I see why people are annoyed. I'm not leaving though, I've tried Apple Music and I always come back.

Premium is the one subscription I never cancel. A dollar more is fine, a month still costs less than an hour of my pay and the ad-free listening is worth it. Hope the cancel and renewal prompts get less annoying with this change.

Didn't see this coming. I already downgraded my app and turned off auto updates to dodge the new layout. Price going up doesn't matter to me, it's the layout. If they force the new layout I'm cancelling the day it happens.

Spotify up a buck while Apple Music gives lossless and Spatial Audio for similar money. Spotify still has Connect and Android Auto, which is the only reason I haven't switched. Price rise makes it harder to justify staying when the UI keeps getting worse.

Paying more for Premium and I still hear podcast ads, which makes no sense. Podcasts are shoved onto the home screen again and there's no way to hide them. Apple Music doesn't do this and YouTube Premium is looking tempting.

Price going up when downloads still break after updates and scrolling my liked songs is slow as hell. Support never fixed it. I'll stay for now since my playlists survive reinstalls, but I'm not paying more for a broken app.

Premium going up and the music tab is still the same awful card layout. I already canceled over the redesign and now I'm switching to Apple Music. Give me album tiles back and I'd come back, but not for more money on this mess.

Doesn't affect me since I'm on free, but I'm still stuck with shuffle-only and ads every few songs. If Premium gets more expensive I'm less likely to ever pay for it. I'll keep using the free playlists.

A dollar more is fine if it actually gets to the artists. Music is still absurdly cheap for what you get, and I'm happy to pay the artists more. The per-stream split is the real problem and this price bump doesn't fix that.
